raw:
In 12 of the 19 races in the 2015 season, the pole sitter (grid 1) won.

I checked each race's top-10 result, which lists each finisher's starting position. The race-by-race outcome:

| Round | Race | Grid 1 | Winner (started) | Pole won? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Australia | Hamilton | Hamilton (1) | Yes |
| 2 | Malaysia | Hamilton | Vettel (2) | No |
| 3 | China | Hamilton | Hamilton (1) | Yes |
| 4 | Bahrain | Hamilton | Hamilton (1) | Yes |
| 5 | Spain | Rosberg | Rosberg (1) | Yes |
| 6 | Monaco | Hamilton | Rosberg (2) | No |
| 7 | Canada | Hamilton | Hamilton (1) | Yes |
| 8 | Austria | Rosberg | Rosberg (2) | No |
| 9 | Britain | Hamilton | Hamilton (1) | Yes |
| 10 | Hungary | Hamilton | Vettel (3) | No |
| 11 | Belgium | Hamilton | Hamilton (1) | Yes |
| 12 | Italy | Hamilton | Hamilton (1) | Yes |
| 13 | Singapore | Vettel | Vettel (1) | Yes |
| 14 | Japan | Rosberg | Hamilton (2) | No |
| 15 | Russia | Rosberg | Hamilton (2) | No |
| 16 | United States | Rosberg | Hamilton (2) | No |
| 17 | Mexico | Rosberg | Rosberg (1) | Yes |
| 18 | Brazil | Rosberg | Rosberg (1) | Yes |
| 19 | Abu Dhabi | Rosberg | Rosberg (1) | Yes |

The grid-1 driver won 12 races and failed to win 7. The win totals match the season standings (Hamilton 10, Rosberg 6, Vettel 3), which confirms the race-by-race outcomes.

ANSWER: 12
